title: tmux: Productive Terminal Workspaces

concepts.title: Status Lines, Themes, and Visual Context

notes: Requester's outline (issue #146) groups the 18 chapters into six parts: I. The Core Model (why-tmux, your-first-tmux-session, sessions-windows-and-panes); II. Everyday Navigation (working-efficiently-in-panes, scrolling-search-and-copy-mode, managing-long-running-work); III. Make tmux Yours (configuration-fundamentals, key-bindings-and-command-mode, status-lines-themes-and-visual-context); IV. Developer Workflows (tmux-for-software-projects, remote-development-with-ssh, reproducible-project-workspaces); V. Automation and Extensions (scripting-tmux, plugins-use-them-deliberately, session-restoration-and-continuity); VI. Advanced Practice (debugging-tmux-problems, collaboration-and-shared-sessions, a-personal-tmux-system). Reflect these part groupings in the table of contents. Each chapter should follow: problem -> concept -> hands-on commands -> realistic workflow -> short exercise -> 'common mistake' callout. tmux-for-software-projects should include worked examples for an Elixir/Phoenix stack (iex -S mix phx.server, tests, logs, mix format) and a Rust stack (editor, cargo watch, tests, docs). Fold the requester's appendix ideas into existing pages rather than separate concept pages: a full command cheat sheet -> cheatsheet.html; an annotated starter tmux.conf -> configuration-fundamentals; general/Elixir/Rust project bootstrap scripts -> reproducible-project-workspaces and scripting-tmux; a migration guide from Terminal tabs/iTerm2/screen/IDE terminals -> why-tmux; a glossary of server/session/client/window/pane/target/format/command-mode terms -> cheatsheet.html.
